title: One machine-readable reading of a drawn tree (ADR-015 amendment 1)
description: The blueprint (docs/proposals/PROPOSAL-agent-framework-blueprint.md, Part VI) draws two trees, UPSTREAM and HOST, as a fixed set of paths that must exist in their drawn place by their drawn name -- the FLOOR, never the ceiling (amendment 1). This is the ONE declaration of that floor for one side; a floor gate is a GENERIC projection of it, never a hand-written list of paths inside an interpreter. A path whose real content belongs to a later link is named `pending` with the link that carries it -- never a fabricated placeholder (Cardinal V).

side.description: Which box of the Part VI drawing this reading is of.

source.description: Where the drawing that this declaration transcribes lives -- file and line range.

path.description: Root-relative, POSIX-formed. A directory path ends in '/'.

drawn_as.description: The label the drawing itself uses for this path, for a reader comparing the two.

pending.description: The link (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, L, or a sub-step of one) whose work gives this path real content. Present only when the path is not yet built for real; its absence from disk is then not a floor failure -- it is printed, not hidden.

holds.description: RECORDS MAP (ADR-015 amendment 8). The kind of truth that lives in this place: the id of one `kinds` row of the record-keeping vocabulary (`record-keeping` schema), never a free word. Declared on a `pending` place too: a place with no content yet still has a declared home, and saying so is the point. Resolved against the vocabulary by `FF-RECORDS-DECLARED`.

writer.description: RECORDS MAP. Who may write this place: the id of one `writers` row of the record-keeping vocabulary.

read_when.description: RECORDS MAP. The retrieval key: the task triggers, in the words a task actually arrives in, that pull this place into context. An agent consults the map by these instead of searching the tree.

lifecycle.description: RECORDS MAP. How this place's content ages and where it goes (its ISO 15489 disposition): the id of one `lifecycles` row of the record-keeping vocabulary.

realised_as.description: ADR-021. The drawn path's truth lives at ANOTHER declared place, by a named decision that says why that form is better. The floor checks the realised path instead of the drawn one. A row is pending OR realised, never both: pending promises to build the drawn form, realised says a decision replaced it.

pending.description: The link that will BUILD the realised form, where the decision is taken and its form not yet built. The drawn form is still never promised: what is pending is the replacement.

declared_by.description: ADR-021. A path BEYOND the drawing, kept because the named decision says it improves the form. Checked like a drawn path; a path beyond the drawing with no row is undeclared.

capability.description: The id of the one capability whose own `installs` puts this path in place. Present only when the path belongs to a capability that is not always enabled; a row with no `capability` always applies. On a host that has not enabled it, the row is skipped and printed as NOT ENABLED, never counted as a floor failure -- read from that capability's own declaration, never restated here.

closed.description: ADR-021 decision 7. Directories this drawing is EXHAUSTIVE at (`.` is the root): every tracked child of one is covered by a row -- drawn, realised or `declared_by` -- or it is undeclared. A directory not named here may hold more than the drawing shows; the drawing is a floor there.
